Therefore, having been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ. —Romans 5:1

...Thru the Bible with Dr. J. Vernon McGee  Exodus 4:6—5:2...

Give God your heart, then let Him sort out the rest. Moses offered some valid reasons proving why he was the wrong guy for the job. God made it clear that as long as Moses had a willing heart, “I will teach you what you shall say.” Follow along as we learn more about Moses’ feelings of inadequacy, Zipporah’s act of faith, and Pharoah’s important question: “Who is the Lord?”

https://www.oneplace.com/ministries/thru-the-bible-with-j-vernon-mcgee/player/exodus-46-52-1292503.html?type=branded#now-playing

https://ttb.org/

...Thru the Bible - Minute with McGee  Dr. J. Vernon McGee...

A tale of three sons

There’s a third son in the parable of the prodigal son. You see, the younger son broke the father’s heart, and the elder son was out of fellowship and without sympathy. But who is the third son? Well, the man who uttered the parable—God’s Son. He’s His ideal Son without sin. He came to a far country, not as a prodigal, but as the Prince of Peace to shed His blood for the sins of the world. And He says, “To as many as receive him, to them gave he the right to become the sons of God,” even to those that don’t do any more nor less than just simply believe in His name.

https://www.oneplace.com/ministries/thru-the-bible-minute-with-mcgee/listen/a-tale-of-three-sons-1292511.html

And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times, [and] strength of salvation: the fear of the LORD [is] his treasure. (Isaiah 33:6)
